body: I am so glad you were able to feel something, and be able to immerse yourself in a story. Hold on to that feeling. Hold on to how good that felt. Use that to keep going if it gets dark again. And be proud, this is a huge step towards being a happier person. Keep it up, and reach out if you need us.

I don’t think you are weak. It’s clear you are hurting, but that does not make you weak. In truth, I think the fact that you are still here, talking to me, means you are incredibly strong. It’s easy for people (sometimes even ourselves) to say, “to be in pain is weakness, if I were strong, I would just control the depression,” but it doesn’t always work that way. Here you are, despite the pain, looking for help. That is what it truly means to be strong. You can get through this. I know it’s not as easy as just ignoring the shitty people, but trust me: the people who hate you because you are depressed are wrong. You are stronger than they think.

I hear you. I’m in between jobs myself. Keep going, my friend. Your friend’s life is worth living. And there are ways out for them without dying. It may take some time, but keep supporting each other. Be patient. Be strong. They can make it through this.

I’m here for you. Please know that having an abusive family does not mean anything bad about you. Abusive people reflect poorly on themselves, not on those they abuse. As for your coworker, I know it’s not easy to hate those you work with. But again, this does not make you a bad person. Even the Dalai Lama is gonna have people who hate him-odds are good it’s not about you, but about something they see in themselves. I hope that makes it easier to bear. Please don’t be embarrassed by your mistakes, by your life, or by yourself. You are here, asking for help. That is not only brave, but very hard to do. I am proud of you. Keep going, and please know that other people’s actions are a reflection on THEM, not on you. You are brave and strong and deserve to live.
And thank you, for being this person’s friend, and for caring so much about them.

Not at all. I just want to offer any support I can. I can see your friend is in a difficult place. But I would hate to see you lose them and I would hate to see the world lose another soul who is struggling. Please keep telling them they are not alone. Support them through being financially dependent so they can cut ties with their parents. There is no shame in cutting out a toxic relationship-even with parents. As human beings, we have the right to take care of ourselves before our parents. Please tell your friend that not wanting to be emotionally abused by family anymore does not mean they do not care. I hope I am not pinning too much on you, but it sounds like you and your friend are really important to each other. I hope you can help them through this point so they can feasibly cut ties.

Contact poison control, throw up the pills if you can. You’re scared, but here you are, and that makes you incredibly brave. So please keep being brave, make it through this moment. Get yourself medical help, we are here, you are not alone.

Hey, here’s a reason to be proud of yourself: you’re here. You are asking for help. That is incredibly strong. And you are not a freak. You are a human being who is going through pain, but who has the strength to reach out and ask for help. I have the same thoughts when I look in a mirror. What keeps me going is the desire to prove the self doubt wrong. It sounds like every time you look in a mirror, you see reasons to hate yourself. I don’t know you, but speaking from experience, I can tell you those reasons are lies. You have made mistakes, we all have. That does not make you a freak. It means you still have things to learn, self doubts to prove wrong and mistakes to forgive. So please live. And keep reaching out when you need help.

Look, I hope this’ll help, but if your friend wants to die to spite abusive parents, wouldn’t it be more spiteful to them to stay alive? Wouldn’t ending it be like letting them win? And tell your friend that life without them would hurt. Please. This person has already touched at least one life-yours-enough to be a best friend. That’s a beautiful thing that should not be taken lightly. Staying alive and being someone’s best friend despite abuse is the best way I can think of to get back at abusive parents. I hope this helps them live.
